title: Actual exam question for Salesforce's Sharing-and-Visibility-Architect exam
question: When you make changes to roles and groups Salesforce locks the entire group membership table, which makes it impossible to process group changes in multiple threads to increase throughput on updates.
suggested_answer: Granular Locking Explanation The term that describes the situation when you make changes to roles and groups Salesforce locks the entire group membership table is Granular Locking. Granular Locking is a feature that improves the concurrency and performance of sharing operations by locking only the affected nodes in the role or territory hierarchy, instead of locking the entire hierarchy. This allows multiple sharing operations to run in parallel without causing lock contention or blocking each other.
